openings.claim: Use an ordinary joint combining fixed insertion stops, corner datums and hand-tightened clamps for both rod positions.
openings.delta: Replace dependence on tight surrounding fit with seating each rod against two plywood datum faces and an M5 insertion-stop bolt before closing a movable plywood clamp plate. Use six plywood pieces for two three-piece pockets; connect pockets with shared fasteners where geometry permits. Keep bolts threaded during release and tether potentially loose plates and hardware with cord. Accommodate 18, 19 and 20 mm rods through clamp travel.
openings.prediction: If connected pockets remain rigid and rods seat consistently, return error will stay within the 2 mm target circle after exchanges and throughout each 10 N, ten-second load. The nearest rival is tight friction fit without deliberate datum seating: it may resist load yet return inconsistently. Smaller return scatter despite clearance favors datum seating; comparable scatter or persistent displacement defeats that explanation. These are unverified predictions.
openings.probe: Within 100 fabrication minutes, make one configuration; verify its envelope fits a 90 mm cube, hardware stays captive, and either rod can be removed by hand. During twenty test minutes, log five exchanges of each rod position, using the 18 mm replacement for the last two exchanges of the 19 mm position. Measure every return and exchange duration; distribute four ten-second 10 N load trials across the sequence. Fail any return or load drift outside the circle, exchange at least forty seconds, or released component. Without a rival configuration, this tests performance but cannot establish comparative causation.
assumptions: Eight bolts suffice for pocket connections, stops and clamps; shared-fastener geometry requires verification.
Available cord can retain release-prone components without obstructing exchange.
Plywood stiffness, contact precision and achievable hand clamping force may be inadequate.

assessment: One ordinary incumbent is proposed. Datums and stops offer plausible positioning, but hardware capacity, geometry and stiffness leave feasibility uncertain. Failure requires rejection or redesign within unchanged constraints.
